This diagram shows two examples of Model Based Add-Ins.  The Add-Ins can be enabled by selecting the ribbon option 'Specialize > Add-Ins > Manage Addin', then placing a tick in the checkbox 'Load on Startup' beside the Add-In that you want to enable.
Model Based Add-Ins are defined within the model, using stereotyped classes.  In this case, the stereotype is 'JavascriptAddin'.  Using these stereotyped classes, you can specify Receptions, Methods and Properties that together define the behaviors of the Add-In, and how it responds to the various events occurring within the system.
Receptions are defined by specifying a signal that will be received.  For this reason, the signals that are relevant to Model Based Add-Ins should be included within the model where you are defining or using Model Based Add-Ins.  You will find the signals that are relevant to Model Based Add-Ins listed on the diagram 'Broadcast Types'.
The Receptions also provide a place to specify JavaScript code that will be executed in response to the receipt of a corresponding signal.  The reception code can also call functions defined as Methods of the class, while the class attributes can be used to define global variables that are available to the executing code.
Model Based Add-Ins

elements.name: EA_Connect
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use EA_Connect events to identify their type and to respond to Enterprise Architect start up. This event occurs when Enterprise Architect first loads your Add-In. Enterprise Architect itself is loading at this time so that while a Repository object is supplied, there is limited information that you can extract from it. The chief uses for EA_Connect are in initializing global Add-In data and for identifying the Add-In as an MDG Add-In. Return Value A string identifying a specialized type of Add-In: User Guide EA_Connect

elements.name: EA_Disconnect
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use the EA_Disconnect event to respond to user requests to disconnect the model branch from an external project. This function is called when Enterprise Architect closes. If you have stored references to Enterprise Architect objects (not recommended anyway), you must release them here. In addition, .NET users must call memory management functions as shown: GC.Collect(); GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers(); Return Value None. User Guide EA_Disconnect

elements.name: EA_GetMenuItems
elements.notes:
The EA_GetMenuItems event enables the Add-In to provide the Enterprise Architect user interface with additional Add-In menu options in various context menus. When a user selects an Add-In menu option, an event is raised and passed back to the Add-In that originally defined that menu option. This event is raised just before Enterprise Architect has to show particular menu options to the user, and its use is described in the Define Menu Items topic. Return Value One of these types:
  • A string indicating the label for a single menu option
  • An array of strings indicating a multiple menu options
  • Empty (Visual Basic/VB.NET) or null (C#) to indicate that no menu should be displayed
In the case of the top-level menu it should be a single string or an array containing only one item, or empty/null. User Guide EA_GetMenuItems

elements.name: EA_GetMenuState
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use the EA_GetMenuState event to set a particular menu option to either enabled or disabled. This is useful when dealing with locked Packages and other situations where it is convenient to show a menu option, but not enable it for use. This event is raised just before Enterprise Architect has to show particular menu options to the user. Its use is further described in the Define Menu Items topic. Return Value None. User Guide EA_GetMenuState

elements.name: EA_GetRibbonCategory
elements.notes:
Add-Ins can use EA_GetRibbonCategory events to identify the Ribbon in which the Add-In should place its menu icon. This event occurs when Enterprise Architect first loads your Add-In. Enterprise Architect itself is loading at this time so that while a Repository object is supplied, there is limited information that you can extract from it. The chief use for EA_GetRibbonCategory is in initializing the Add-In access point. Return Value A string matching the name of the selected ribbon (in English if you are using a translated version). The possible names are:
  • Start
  • Design
  • Layout
  • Publish
  • Specialize
  • Construct
  • Code
  • Simulate
  • Execute
  • Manage
It is not possible to include Add-Ins in the 'Specification - Specify' ribbon or 'Documentation - Edit' ribbon. If the function isn't implemented (or if an invalid name is returned) the 'Add-In' menu will be available from the 'Specialize' ribbon, 'Add-Ins' panel. User Guide EA_GetRibbonCategory

elements.name: EA_MenuClick
elements.notes: EA_MenuClick events are received by an Add-In in response to user selection of a menu option. The event is raised when the user clicks on a particular menu option. When a user clicks on one of your non-parent menu options, your Add-In receives a MenuClick event, defined as: Sub EA_MenuClick(Repository As EA.Repository, ByVal MenuLocation As String, ByVal MenuName As String, ByVal ItemName As String) This code is an example of use: If MenuName = "-&Diagram" And ItemName = "&Properties" then MsgBox Repository.GetCurrentDiagram.Name, vbInformation Else MsgBox "Not Implemented", vbCritical End If Notice that your code can directly access Enterprise Architect data and UI elements using Repository methods. Return Value None. User Guide EA_MenuClick

elements.name: EA_OnAddinPropertiesTabChanging
elements.notes:
The list of properties that will be available in this broadcast:
  • TabName - The name of the Add-Ins window tab changing
  • PropID - Unique ID assign to Property item.
  • ChangeValue - The value the Property is changing to.
  • OriginalValue - The original value assigned to the Property

elements.name: EA_OnOutputItemClicked
elements.notes: EA_OnOutputItemClicked events inform Add-Ins that the user has clicked on a list entry in the system tab or one of the user defined output tabs. Usually an Add-In responds to this event in order to capture activity on an output tab they had previously created through a call to Repository.AddTab(). Note that every loaded Add-In receives this event for every click on an output tab in Enterprise Architect, irrespective of whether the Add-In created that tab. Add-Ins should therefore check the TabName parameter supplied by this event to ensure that they are not responding to other Add-Ins' events. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnOutputItemClicked

elements.name: EA_OnOutputItemDoubleClicked
elements.notes: EA_OnOutputItemDoubleClicked events inform Add-Ins that the user has used the mouse to double-click on a list entry in one of the user-defined output tabs. Usually an Add-In responds to this event in order to capture activity on an output tab they had previously created through a call to Repository.AddTab(). Note that every loaded Add-In receives this event for every double-click on an output tab in Enterprise Architect, irrespective of whether the Add-In created that tab; Add-Ins should therefore check the TabName parameter supplied by this event to ensure that they are not responding to other Add-Ins' events. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnOutputItemDoubleClicked

elements.name: EA_ShowHelp
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use the EA_ShowHelp event to show a Help topic for a particular menu option. When the user has an Add-In menu option selected, pressing F1 can be related to the required Help topic by the Add-In and a suitable Help message shown. This event is raised when the user presses F1 on a menu option that is not a parent menu. Return Value None. User Guide EA_ShowHelp

elements.name: EA_FileClose
elements.notes: The EA_FileClose event enables the Add-In to respond to a File Close event. When Enterprise Architect closes an opened Model file, this event is raised and passed to all Add-Ins implementing this method. This event occurs when the model currently opened within Enterprise Architect is about to be closed (when another model is about to be opened or when Enterprise Architect is about to shutdown). Return Value None. User Guide EA_FileClose

elements.name: EA_FileNew
elements.notes: The EA_FileNew event enables the Add-In to respond to a File New event. When Enterprise Architect creates a new model file, this event is raised and passed to all Add-Ins implementing this method. The event occurs when the model being viewed by the Enterprise Architect user changes, for whatever reason (through user interaction or Add-In activity). Return Value None. User Guide EA_FileNew

elements.name: EA_FileOpen
elements.notes: The EA_FileOpen event enables the Add-In to respond to a File Open event. When Enterprise Architect opens a new model file, this event is raised and passed to all Add-Ins implementing this method. The event occurs when the model being viewed by the Enterprise Architect user changes, for whatever reason (through user interaction or Add-In activity). Return Value None. User Guide EA_FileOpen

elements.name: EA_OnPostCloseDiagram
elements.notes: EA_OnPostCloseDiagram notifies Add-Ins that a diagram has been closed. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnPostCloseDiagram

elements.name: EA_OnPostInitialized
elements.notes: EA_OnPostInitialized notifies Add-Ins that the Repository object has finished loading and any necessary initialization steps can now be performed on the object. For example, the Add-In can create an 'Output' tab using Repository.CreateOutputTab. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnPostInitialized

elements.name: EA_OnPostOpenDiagram
elements.notes: EA_OnPostOpenDiagram notifies Add-Ins that a diagram has been opened. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnPostOpenDiagram

elements.name: EA_OnPostTransform
elements.notes: EA_OnPostTransform notifies Add-Ins that an MDG transformation has taken place with the output in the specified target Package. This event occurs when a user runs an MDG transform on one or more target Packages; the notification is provided for each transform/target Package immediately after all transform processes have completed. Return Value Reserved for future use. User Guide EA_OnPostTransform

elements.name: EA_OnPreExitInstance
elements.notes: EA_OnPreExitInstance is not currently used. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnPreExitInstance

elements.name: EA_OnRetrieveModelTemplate
elements.notes: EA_OnRetrieveModelTemplate requests that an Add-In pass a model template to Enterprise Architect. This event occurs when a user executes the 'Add a New Model Using Wizard' command to add a model that has been defined by an MDG Technology. Return Value Return a string containing the XMI export of the model that is being used as a template. Return an empty string if access to the template is denied; the Add-In is to handle user notification of the error. User Guide EA_OnRetrieveModelTemplate

elements.name: EA_OnTabChanged
elements.notes: EA_OnTabChanged notifies Add-Ins that the currently open tab has changed. Diagrams do not generate the message when they are first opened - use the broadcast event EA_OnPostOpenDiagram for this purpose. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnTabChanged

elements.name: EA_AddinLicenseGetDescription
elements.notes: Before the Enterprise Architect 'License Management' dialog is displayed, EA_AddInLicenseGetDescription is sent once for each Add-In key to the first Add-In that elected to handle that key. The value returned by EA_AddinLicenseGetDescription is used as the key's plain text description. Return Value A String containing a plain text description of the provided AddinKey. User Guide EA_AddinLicenseGetDescription

elements.name: EA_AddinLicenseValidate
elements.notes: When a user directly enters into the 'License Management' dialog a license key that doesn't match a Sparx Systems key, EA_AddInLicenseValidate is broadcast to all Enterprise Architect Add-Ins, providing them with a chance to use the Add-In key to determine the level of functionality to provide. When a key is retrieved from the Sparx Systems Keystore only the target Add-In will be called with the key. For the Add-In to validate itself against this key, the Add-In's EA_AddinLicenseValidate handler should return confirmation that the license has been validated. As the EA_AddinLicenseValidate event is broadcast to all Add-Ins, one license can validate many Add-Ins. If an Add-In elects to handle a license key by returning a confirmation to EA_AddinLicenseValidate, it is called upon to provide a description of the license key through the EA_AddinLicenseGetDescription event. If more than one Add-In elects to handle a license key, the first Add-In that returns a confirmation to EA_AddinLicenseValidate is queried for the license key description. Return Value Returns True if the license key is validated for the current Add-In. Returns False otherwise. User Guide EA_AddinLicenseValidate

elements.name: EA_GetSharedAddinName
elements.notes: As an Add-In writer you can distribute keys to your Add-In via the Enterprise Architect Keystore, provided that your keys are added using a prefix that allows the system to identify the Add-In to which they belong. EA_GetSharedAddinName is called to determine what prefix the Add-In is using. If a matching key is found in the keystore the 'License Management' dialog will display the name returned by EA_AddinLicenseGetDescription to your users. Finally, when the user selects a key, that key will be passed to your Add-In to validate by calling EA_AddinLicenseValidate. Return Value A String containing a product name code for the provided Add-In, such as MYADDIN. This will be shown in plain text in any keys added to the keystore. User Guide EA_GetSharedAddinName

elements.name: EA_GetCompartmentData
elements.notes: This event occurs when Enterprise Architect is instructed to redraw an element. It requests that the Add-In provide the data to populate the element's compartment. Return Value A variant containing a formatted string. The format is illustrated in this example: User Guide EA_GetCompartmentData

elements.name: EA_QueryAvailableCompartments
elements.notes: This event occurs when Enterprise Architect's diagrams are refreshed. It is a request for the Add-In to provide a list of user-defined compartments. The EA_GetCompartmentData event then queries each object for the data to display in each user-defined compartment. Return Value A String containing a comma-separated list of user-defined compartments. User Guide EA_QueryAvailableCompartments

elements.name: EA_OnContextItemChanged
elements.notes: EA_OnContextItemChanged notifies Add-Ins that a different item is now in context. This event occurs after a user has selected an item anywhere in the Enterprise Architect GUI. Add-Ins that require knowledge of the current item in context can subscribe to this broadcast function. If ot = otRepository, then this function behaves in the same way as EA_FileOpen. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnContextItemChanged

elements.name: EA_OnContextItemDoubleClicked
elements.notes: EA_OnContextItemDoubleClicked notifies Add-Ins that the user has double-clicked the item currently in context. This event occurs when a user has double-clicked (or pressed the Enter key) on the item in context, either in a diagram, in the Browser window or in a custom compartment. Add-Ins to handle events can subscribe to this broadcast function. Return Value Return True to notify Enterprise Architect that the double-click event has been handled by an Add-In. Return False to enable Enterprise Architect to continue processing the event. User Guide EA_OnContextItemDoubleClicked

elements.name: EA_OnNotifyContextItemModified
elements.notes: EA_OnNotifyContextItemModified notifies Add-Ins that the current context item has been modified. This event occurs when a user has modified the context item. Add-Ins that require knowledge of when an item has been modified can subscribe to this broadcast function. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnNotifyContextItemModified

elements.name: EA_OnCustomTableBeginEdit
elements.notes: EA_OnCustomTableBeginEdit notifies Add-Ins that the Custom Table is beginning edit mode. This broadcast event can only be enabled by the Custom Table's 'script' Tagged Value. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnCustomTableBeginEdit

elements.name: EA_OnCustomTableCellUpdated
elements.notes: EA_OnCustomTableCellUpdated notifies Add-Ins that a cell value has been updated. This broadcast event can only be enabled by the Custom Table's 'script' Tagged Value. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnCustomTableCellUpdated

elements.name: EA_OnCustomTableEndEdit
elements.notes:
EA_OnCustomTableEndEdit notifies Add-Ins that an Custom Table element is ending edit mode. This broadcast event can only be enabled by the Custom Table's 'script' Tagged Value. Return Value This function allows validation of the table data, and returns a Boolean value:
  • true to save the current data in the grid, or
  • false to abandon the current data
User Guide EA_OnCustomTableEndEdit

elements.name: EA_OnCustomTableSelectionChanged
elements.notes: EA_OnCustomTableSelectionChanged notifies Add-Ins that a cell of the Custom Table has changed. This broadcast event can only be enabled by the Custom Table's 'script' Tagged Value. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnCustomTableSelectionChanged

elements.name: EA_OnEndValidation
elements.notes: EA_OnEndValidation notifies Add-Ins that model validation has completed. Use this event to arrange any clean-up operations arising from the validation. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnEndValidation

elements.name: EA_OnInitializeUserRules
elements.notes: EA_OnInitializeUserRules is called on Enterprise Architect start-up and requests that the Add-In provide Enterprise Architect with a rule category and list of rule IDs for model validation. This function must be implemented by any Add-In that is to perform its own model validation. It must call Project.DefineRuleCategory once and Project.DefineRule for each rule; these functions are described in the Project Interface topic. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnInitializeUserRules

elements.name: EA_OnRunAttributeRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each attribute in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given attribute, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunAttributeRule

elements.name: EA_OnRunConnectorRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each connector in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given connector, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunConnectorRule

elements.name: EA_OnRunDiagramRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each diagram in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given diagram, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunDiagramRule

elements.name: EA_OnRunElementRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each element in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given element, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunElementRule

elements.name: EA_OnRunMethodRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each method in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given method, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunMethodRule

elements.name: EA_OnRunPackageRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each Package in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given Package, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunPackageRule

elements.name: EA_OnRunParameterRule
elements.notes: This event is triggered once for each rule defined in EA_OnInitializeUserRules to be performed on each parameter in the selection being validated. If you don't want to perform the rule defined by RuleID on the given parameter, then simply return without performing any action. On performing any validation, if a validation error is found, use the Repository.ProjectInterface.PublishResult method to notify Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnRunParameterRule

elements.name: EA_OnStartValidation
elements.notes: EA_OnStartValidation notifies Add-Ins that a user has invoked the model validation command from Enterprise Architect. Return Value None. User Guide EA_OnStartValidation

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewAttribute
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewAttribute notifies Add-Ins that a new attribute has been created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to modify the attribute upon creation. This event occurs when a user creates a new attribute on an element by either drag-and-dropping from the Browser window, using the 'Attributes' tab of the Features window, or using the in-place editor on the diagram. The notification is provided immediately after the attribute is created. Return Value Return True if the attribute has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewAttribute

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewConnector
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewConnector notifies Add-Ins that a new connector has been created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to modify the connector upon creation. This event occurs after a user has dragged a new connector from the Toolbox or Resources window onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately after the connector is added to the model. Return Value Return True if the connector has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewConnector

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewDiagram
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewDiagram notifies Add-Ins that a new diagram has been created. It enables Add-Ins to modify the diagram upon creation. Return Value Return True if the diagram has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewDiagram

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewDiagramObject
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewDiagramObject notifies Add-Ins that a new object has been created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to modify the object upon creation. This event occurs after a user has dragged a new object from the Project Browser or Resources window onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately after the object is added to the diagram. Return Value Return True if the element has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewDiagramObject

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewElement
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewElement notifies Add-Ins that a new element has been created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to modify the element upon creation. This event occurs after a user has dragged a new element from the Toolbox or Resources window onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately after the element is added to the model. Set Repository.SuppressEADialogs to True to suppress Enterprise Architect from showing its default 'Properties' dialog. Return Value Return True if the element has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewElement

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewGlossaryTerm
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewGlossaryTerm notifies Add-Ins that a new glossary term has been created. It enables Add-Ins to modify the glossary term upon creation. The notification is provided immediately after the glossary term is added to the model. Return Value Return True if the glossary term has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewGlossaryTerm

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewMethod
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewMethod notifies Add-Ins that a new method has been created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to modify the method upon creation. This event occurs when a user creates a new method on an element by either drag-dropping from the Project Browser, using the method's 'Properties' dialog, or using the in-place editor on the diagram. The notification is provided immediately after the method is created. Return Value Return True if the method has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewMethod

elements.name: EA_OnPostNewPackage
elements.notes: EA_OnPostNewPackage notifies Add-Ins that a new Package has been created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to modify the Package upon creation. This event occurs when a user drags a new Package from the Toolbox or Resources window onto a diagram, or by selecting the New Package icon from the Project Browser. Return Value Return True if the Package has been updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostNewPackage

elements.name: EA_OnPreDropFromTree
elements.notes: When a user drags any kind of element from the Project Browser onto a diagram, EA_OnPreDropFromTree notifies the Add-In that a new item is about to be dropped onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the element is dropped, so that the Add-In can override the default action that would be taken for this drag. Return Value Return True to allow the default behavior to be executed. Return False if you are overriding this behavior. User Guide EA_OnPreDropFromTree

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewAttribute
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewAttribute notifies Add-Ins that a new attribute is about to be created on an element. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new attribute. This event occurs when a user creates a new attribute on an element by either drag-dropping from the Browser window, using the 'Attributes' tab of the Features window, or using the in-place editor on the diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the attribute is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the attribute. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new attribute to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new attribute. User Guide EA_OnPreNewAttribute

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewConnector
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewConnector notifies Add-Ins that a new connector is about to be created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of a new connector. This event occurs when a user drags a new connector from the Toolbox or Resources window, onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the connector is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the connector. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new connector to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new connector. User Guide EA_OnPreNewConnector

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewDiagram
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewDiagram notifies Add-Ins that a new diagram is about to be created. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the diagram is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the diagram. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new diagram to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new diagram. User Guide EA_OnPreNewDiagram

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewDiagramObject
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewDiagramObject notifies Add-Ins that a new diagram object is about to be dropped on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new object. This event occurs when a user drags an object from the Enterprise Architect Project Browser or Resources window onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the object is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the object. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the object to the model. Return False to disable addition of the object. User Guide EA_OnPreNewDiagramObject

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewElement
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewElement notifies Add-Ins that a new element is about to be created on a diagram. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new element. This event occurs when a user drags a new element from the Toolbox or Resources window onto a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the element is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the element. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new element to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new element. User Guide EA_OnPreNewElement

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewGlossaryTerm
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewGlossaryTerm notifies Add-Ins that a new glossary term is about to be created. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new glossary term. The notification is provided immediately before the glossary term is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the element. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new glossary term to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new glossary term. User Guide EA_OnPreNewGlossaryTerm

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewMethod
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewMethod notifies Add-Ins that a new method is about to be created on an element. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new method. This event occurs when a user creates a new method on an element by either drag-dropping from the Browser window, using the 'Operations' tab of the Features window, or using the in-place editor on the diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the method is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the method. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new method to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new method. User Guide EA_OnPreNewMethod

elements.name: EA_OnPreNewPackage
elements.notes: EA_OnPreNewPackage notifies Add-Ins that a new Package is about to be created in the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny creation of the new Package. This event occurs when a user drags a new Package from the Toolbox or Resources window onto a diagram, or by selecting the New Package icon from the Project Browser. The notification is provided immediately before the Package is created, so that the Add-In can disable addition of the Package. Return Value Return True to enable addition of the new Package to the model. Return False to disable addition of the new Package. User Guide EA_OnPreNewPackage

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteAttribute
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteAttribute notifies Add-Ins that an attribute is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the attribute. This event occurs when a user attempts to permanently delete an attribute from the Project Browser. The notification is provided immediately before the attribute is deleted, so that the Add-In can disable deletion of the attribute. Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the attribute from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the attribute. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteAttribute

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteConnector
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteConnector notifies Add-Ins that a connector is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the connector. This event occurs when a user attempts to permanently delete a connector on a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the connector is deleted, so that the Add-In can disable deletion of the connector. Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the connector from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the connector. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteConnector

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteDiagram
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteDiagram notifies Add-Ins that a diagram is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the diagram. This event occurs when a user attempts to permanently delete a diagram from the Project Browser. The notification is provided immediately before the diagram is deleted, so that the Add-In can disable deletion of the diagram. Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the diagram from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the diagram. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteDiagram

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteDiagramObject
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteDiagramObject notifies Add-Ins that a diagram object is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the element. This event occurs when a user attempts to permanently delete an element from a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the element is deleted, so that the Add-In can disable deletion of the element. Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the element from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the element. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteDiagramObject

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteElement
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteElement notifies Add-Ins that an element is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the element. This event occurs when a user deletes an element from the Project Browser or on a diagram. The notification is provided immediately before the element is deleted, so that the Add-In can disable deletion of the element. Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the element from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the element. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteElement

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteGlossaryTerm
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteGlossaryTerm notifies Add-Ins that a glossary term is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the glossary term. The notification is provided immediately before the glossary term is deleted, so that the Add-In can disable deletion of the glossary term. Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the glossary term from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the glossary term. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteGlossaryTerm

elements.name: EA_OnPreDeleteMethod
elements.notes: EA_OnPreDeleteMethod notifies Add-Ins that a method (operation) is to be deleted from the model. It enables Add-Ins to permit or deny deletion of the method. This event occurs when a user attempts to permanently delete a method from the Project Browser. Return False to disable deletion of the method. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteMethod

elements.notes: EA_OnInitializeTechnologies requests that an Add-In pass an MDG Technology to Enterprise Architect for loading. This event occurs on Enterprise Architect startup. Return your technology XML to this function and Enterprise Architect loads and enables it. Return Value Return the MDG Technology as a single XML string. User Guide EA_OnInitializeTechnologies

elements.name: EA_OnPostActivateTechnology
elements.notes: EA_OnPostActivateTechnology notifies Add-Ins that an MDG Technology resource has been activated in the model. This event occurs when a user activates an MDG Technology resource in the model (by clicking on the Set Active button on the 'MDG Technologies' dialog, or by selecting the technology in the list box in the Default Tools toolbar). The notification is provided immediately after the user succeeds in activating the MDG Technology, so that the Add-In can update the Technology if necessary. Return Value Return True if the MDG Technology resource is updated during this notification. Return False otherwise. User Guide EA_OnPostActivateTechnology

elements.name: EA_OnPreActivateTechnology
elements.notes: EA_OnPreActivateTechnology notifies Add-Ins that an MDG Technology resource is about to be activated in the model. This event occurs when a user selects to activate an MDG Technology resource in the model (by clicking on the Set Active button on the 'MDG Technologies' dialog or by selecting the technology in the list box in the Default Tools toolbar). The notification is provided immediately after the user attempts to activate the MDG Technology, so that the Add-In can permit or disable activation of the Technology. Return Value Return True to enable activation of the MDG Technology resource in the model. Return False to disable activation of the MDG Technology resource. User Guide EA_OnPreActivateTechnology

Return Value Return True to enable deletion of the MDG Technology resource from the model. Return False to disable deletion of the MDG Technology resource. User Guide EA_OnPreDeleteTechnology

elements.name: MDG_BuildProject
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_BuildProject to handle file changes caused by generation. This function is called in response to a user selecting the 'Execute > Run > Build > Build' ribbon option. Respond to this event by compiling the project source files into a running application. Return Value None. User Guide MDG_BuildProject

elements.name: MDG_Connect
elements.notes: An Add-In uses MDG_Connect to handle a user driven request to connect a model branch to an external application. The function is called when the user attempts to connect a particular Enterprise Architect Package to an as yet unspecified external project. The Add-In calls the event to interact with the user to specify such a project. The Add-In is responsible for retaining the connection details, which should be stored on a per-user or per-workstation basis. That is, users who share a common Enterprise Architect model over a network should be able to connect and disconnect to external projects independently of one another. The Add-In should therefore not store connection details in an Enterprise Architect repository. A suitable place to store such details would be: SHGetFolderPath(..CSIDL_APPDATA..)\AddinName The PackageGuid parameter is the same identifier as is required for most events relating to the MDG Add-In. Therefore it is recommended that the connection details be indexed using the PackageGuid value. The PackageID parameter is provided to aid fast retrieval of Package details from Enterprise Architect, should this be required. Return Value Returns a non-zero to indicate that a connection has been made; a zero indicates that the user has not nominated a project and connection should not proceed. User Guide MDG_Connect

elements.name: MDG_Disconnect
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_Disconnect to respond to user requests to disconnect the model branch from an external project. This function is called when the user attempts to disconnect an associated external project. The Add-In is required to delete the details of the connection. Return Value Returns a non-zero to indicate that a disconnection has occurred enabling Enterprise Architect to update the user interface. A zero indicates that the user has not disconnected from an external project. User Guide MDG_Disconnect

elements.name: MDG_GetConnectedPackages
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_GetConnectedPackages to return a list of current connections between Enterprise Architect and an external application. This function is called when the Add-In is first loaded, and is expected to return a list of the available connections to external projects for this Add-In. Return Value Returns an array of GUID strings representing individual Enterprise Architect Packages. User Guide MDG_GetConnectedPackages

elements.name: MDG_GetProperty
elements.notes:
MDG_GetProperty provides miscellaneous Add-In details to Enterprise Architect. This function is called by Enterprise Architect to poll the Add-In for information relating to the PropertyName. This event should occur in as short a duration as possible, as Enterprise Architect does not cache the information provided by the function. Values corresponding to these PropertyNames must be provided:
  • IconID - Return the name of a DLL and a resource identifier in the format #ResID, where the resource ID indicates an icon c:\program files\myapp\myapp.dlll#101
  • Language - Return the default language that Classes should be assigned when they are created in Enterprise Architect
  • HiddenMenus - Return one or more values from the MDGMenus enumeration to hide menus that do not apply to your Add-In if(PropertyName == "HiddenMenus")
return mgBuildProject + mgRun; Return Value See the start of this topic. User Guide MDG_GetProperty

elements.name: MDG_Merge
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_Merge to jointly handle changes to both the model branch and the code project that the model branch is connected to. This event should be called whenever the user has asked to merge their model branch with its connected code project, or whenever the user has established a new connection to a code project. The purpose of this event is to make the Add-In interact with the user to perform a merge between the model branch and the connected project. Return Value Return a non-zero if the merge operation completed successfully and a zero value when the operation has been unsuccessful. User Guide MDG_Merge

elements.name: MDG_NewClass
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_NewClass to alter details of a Class before it is created. This method is called when Enterprise Architect generates a new Class, and requires information relating to assigning the language and file path. The file path should be passed back as a return value and the language should be passed back via the language parameter. Return Value Returns a string containing the file path that should be assigned to the Class. User Guide MDG_NewClass

elements.name: MDG_PostGenerate
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_PostGenerate to handle file changes caused by generation. This event is called after Enterprise Architect has prepared text to replace the existing contents of a file. Responding to this event enables the Add-In to write to the linked application's user interface rather than modify the file directly. When the contents of a file are changed, Enterprise Architect passes FileContents as a non-empty string. New files created as a result of code generation are also sent through this mechanism, so the Add-Ins can add new files to the linked project's file list. When new files are created Enterprise Architect passes FileContents as an empty string. When a non-zero is returned by this function, the Add-In has successfully written the contents of the file. A zero value for the return indicates to Enterprise Architect that the file must be saved. Return Value The return value depends on the type of event that this function is responding to (see introduction). This function is required to handle two separate and distinct cases. User Guide MDG_PostGenerate

elements.name: MDG_PostMerge
elements.notes: MDG_PostMerge is called by Enterprise Architect after a merge process has been completed. File save checking should not be performed with this function, but should be handled by MDG_PreGenerate, MDG_PostGenerate and MDG_PreReverse. Return Value Return a zero value if the post-merge process has failed. A non-zero return indicates that the post-merge has been successful. Enterprise Architect assumes a non-zero return if this method is not implemented. User Guide MDG_PostMerge

elements.name: MDG_PreGenerate
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_PreGenerate to deal with unsaved changes. This function is called immediately before Enterprise Architect attempts to generate files from the model. A possible use of this function would be to prompt the user to save unsaved source files. Return Value Return a zero value to abort generation. Any other value enables the generation to continue. User Guide MDG_PreGenerate

elements.name: MDG_PreMerge
elements.notes: MDG_PreMerge is called after a merge process has been initiated by the user and before Enterprise Architect performs the merge process. This event is called after a user has performed their interactions with the merge screen and has confirmed the merge with the OK button, but before Enterprise Architect performs the merge process using the data provided by the MDG_Merge call, before any changes have been made to the model or the connected project. This event is made available to provide the Add-In with the opportunity to generally set internal Add-In flags to augment the MDG_PreGenerate, MDG_PostGenerate and MDG_PreReverse events. File save checking should not be performed with this function, but should be handled by MDG_PreGenerate, MDG_PostGenerate and MDG_PreReverse. Return Value A return value of zero indicates that the merge process can not occur. If the value is not zero the merge process proceeds. If this method is not implemented then it is assumed that a merge process is used. User Guide MDG_PreMerge

elements.name: MDG_PreReverse
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_PreReverse to save file changes before they are imported into Enterprise Architect. This function operates on a list of files that are about to be reverse-engineered into Enterprise Architect. If the user is working on unsaved versions of these files in an editor, you could either prompt the user or save automatically. Return Value None. User Guide MDG_PreReverse

elements.name: MDG_RunExe
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_RunExe to run the target application. This function is called when the user selects the 'Execute > Run > Start > Run' ribbon option. Respond to this event by launching the compiled application. Return Value None. User Guide MDG_RunExe

elements.name: MDG_View
elements.notes: Add-Ins can use MDG_View to display user specified code elements. This function is called by Enterprise Architect when the user asks to view a particular code element. The Add-In can then present that element in its own way, usually in a code editor. Return Value Return a non-zero value to indicate that the Add-In has processed the request. Returning a zero value results in Enterprise Architect employing the standard viewing process, which is to launch the associated source file. User Guide MDG_View

Modeling Tips This BKM defines 4 parameters:
  • Product Type : string
  • Rate : number
  • Term : number
  • Amount : number
The function body is implemented as Context in Boxed Notation.
  • Local variable "Monthly Fee" is evaluated by a "if...else if...else" statement
  • Local variable "Monthly Repayment" is evaluated by a built in function "PMT".
  • The return value is formatted by built in function "decimal"
Simulation Provide the "Values for Simulation Parameters" as follows:
  • "STANDARD LOAN"
  • 0.045/12
  • 12 * 30
  • 300000
Save, Validate and Run. The results will be rendered on the Context.

The Simple Model: Calculate the difference of two squares. For example, provided a = 5, b = 3; the difference of squares is: a^2 - b^2 = 25 - 9 = 16 We can also solve this problem in a polynomial factoring way. (a + b) * (a - b) BKM Addition/Subtraction/Multiplication These 3 BKMs' accept two parameters and return a result calculated from a logic implemented as literal expression. Invocation & parameter binding The 3 BKMs (Addition/Subtraction/Multiplication) are modeled to be reused by other BKMs or Decisions through invocation. The caller will bind the parameters with values and retrieve the result. Simulation Tips Provide the "Values for Simulation Parameters" as follows:
  • a: 5
  • b: 3
Validate the model and run the simulation. We expect number 16 be returned. The runtime simulation results will be showing on in the Invocation

Modeling Tips This BKM defines 3 parameters:
  • Rate : number
  • Term : number
  • Principle : number
The function body is implemented as Literal Expression
  • calculates the payment for a loan based on constant payments and a constant interest rate
Example Given a home loan with amount of 300000 for 30 years, at the annual interest rate of 4%; What is the MONTHLY repayment? Provide the "Values for Simulation Parameters" as follows:
  • Rate: 0.04 / 12
  • Term: 30 * 12
  • Principle: 300000
Validate the model and run the simulation. The result is 1432.25 (NOTE: the expression used built-in function "decimal" to format the floating result.) The runtime simulation results will be showing on in the Literal Expression.

elements.name: Affordability calculation
elements.notes: The Affordability calculation decision logic defines a boxed function deriving Affordability from Monthly Income, Monthly Repayments, Monthly Expenses and Required Monthly Installment. One step in this calculation derives Credit contingency factor by invoking the Credit contingency factor table business

elements.name: Application risk score
elements.notes: The Application Risk Score decision logic invokes the Application risk score model business knowledge model, passing Applicant data.Age as the Age parameter, Applicant data.MaritalStatus as the Marital Status parameter and Applicant data.EmploymentStatus as the Employment Status parameter.

elements.name: Application risk score model
elements.notes: The Application risk score model decision logic defines a complete, no-order multiple-hit table with aggregation, deriving Application risk score from Age, Marital Status and Employment Status, as the sum of the Partial scores of all matching rows (this is therefore a predictive scorecard represented as a decision table).

elements.name: Bureau call type
elements.notes: The Bureau call type decision logic invokes the Bureau call type table, passing the output of the Pre-bureau risk category decision as the Pre-Bureau Risk Category parameter.

elements.name: Bureau call type table
elements.notes: The Bureau call type table decision logic defines a complete, unique-hit decision table deriving Bureau Call Type from Pre-Bureau Risk Category.

elements.name: Credit contingency factor table
elements.notes: The Credit contingency factor table decision logic defines a complete, unique-hit decision table deriving Credit contingency factor from Risk Category.

elements.name: Eligibility
elements.notes: The Eligibility decision logic invokes the Eligibility rules business knowledge model, passing Applicant data.Age as the Age parameter, the output of the Pre-bureau risk category decision as the Pre-Bureau Risk Category parameter, and the output of the Pre-bureau affordability decision as the Pre-Bureau Affordability parameter.

elements.name: Eligibility rules
elements.notes: The Eligibility rules decision logic defines a complete, priority-ordered single hit decision table deriving Eligibility from Pre-Bureau Risk Category, Pre-Bureau Affordability and Age.

elements.name: Installment calculation
elements.notes: The Installment calculation decision logic defines a boxed function deriving monthly installment from Product Type, Rate, Term and Amount.

elements.name: Post-bureau affordability
elements.notes: The Post-bureau affordability decision logic invokes the Affordability calculation business knowledge model, passing Applicant data.Monthly.Income as the Monthly Income parameter, Applicant data.Monthly.Repayments as the Monthly Repayments parameter, Applicant data.Monthly.Expenses as the Monthly Expenses parameter, the output of the Post-bureau risk category decision as the Risk Category parameter, and the output of the Required monthly installment decision as the Required Monthly Installment parameter.

elements.name: Post-bureau risk category
elements.notes: The Post-bureau risk category decision logic invokes the Post-bureau risk category business knowledge model, passing Applicant data.ExistingCustomer as the Existing Customer parameter, Bureau data.CreditScore as the Credit Score parameter, and the output of the Application risk score decision as the Application Risk Score parameter. Note that if Bureau data is null (due to the THROUGH strategy bypassing the Collect bureau data task) the Credit Score parameter will be null.

elements.name: Post-bureau risk category table
elements.notes: The Post-bureau risk category table decision logic defines a complete, unique-hit decision table deriving Post-Bureau Risk Category from Existing Customer, Application Risk Score and Credit Score.

elements.name: Pre-bureau affordability
elements.notes: The Pre-bureau affordability decision logic invokes the Affordability calculation business knowledge model, passing Applicant data.Monthly.Income as the Monthly Income parameter, Applicant data.Monthly.Repayments as the Monthly Repayments parameter, Applicant data.Monthly.Expenses as the Monthly Expenses parameter, the output of the Pre-bureau risk category decision as the Risk Category parameter, and the output of the Required monthly installment decision as the Required Monthly Installment parameter.

elements.name: Pre-bureau risk category
elements.notes: The Pre-Bureau Risk Category decision logic invokes the Pre-bureau risk category table business knowledge model, passing Applicant data.ExistingCustomer as the Existing Customer parameter and the output of the Application risk score decision as the Application Risk Score parameter.

elements.name: Pre-bureau risk category table
elements.notes: The Pre-bureau risk category table decision logic defines a complete, unique-hit decision table deriving Pre-bureau risk category from Existing Customer and Application Risk Score.

elements.name: Required monthly installment
elements.notes: The Required monthly installment decision logic invokes the Installment calculation business knowledge model, passing Requested product.ProductType as the Product Type parameter, Requested product.Rate as the Rate parameter, Requested product.Term as the Term parameter, and Requested product.Amount as the Amount parameter.

elements.name: Routing
elements.notes: The Routing decision logic invokes the Routing rules business knowledge model, passing Bureau data . Bankrupt as the Bankrupt parameter, Bureau data . CreditScore as the Credit Score parameter, the output of the Post-bureau risk category decision as the Post-Bureau Risk Category parameter, and the output of the Post-bureau affordability decision as the Post-Bureau Affordability parameter. Note that if Bureau data is null (due to the THROUGH strategy bypassing the Collect bureau data task) the Bankrupt and Credit Score parameters will be null.

elements.name: Routing rules
elements.notes: The Routing Rules decision logic defines a complete, priority-ordered single hit decision table deriving Routing from Post-Bureau Risk Category, Post-Bureau Affordability, Bankrupt and Credit Score.

elements.name: Strategy
elements.notes: The Strategy decision logic defines a complete, unique-hit decision table deriving Strategy from Eligibility and Bureau call type.

The Music Player package demonstrates a number of advanced features for StateMachine simulation.

The 'Player State' StateMachine represents the core behavior of the Music Player class. Notice that the On state is divided into two concurrent regions, each containing a number of sub-states. The first of these regions, named Play State, controls loading and playing the songs. Upon entry of the On state, the Play State region enters the Load state. The Load state's entry action loads the SongList and PlayLists. Once this is complete, this region transitions to the Standby state. In the Standby state, the simulation waits for a trigger, either PlaySong or PlayList, to transition out of Standby. In this example, each of the transitions exiting the Standby state performs a Transition Action, in which they assign a string argument to an internal variable (the Song title or the PlayList name). The second concurrent region, Repeat Mode, controls the player's repeat behavior. At any time during simulation, you can change the Repeat Mode, by sending the SetRepeat trigger. Transitions in the Play State region use Guard conditions that test the Repeat Mode state to determine whether the transition is allowed. At any time during simulation, the simulator will accept the Stop signal to return to Standby, or the PowerOff signal to end the simulation.
The 'All' playlist is defined.

Some of the things that you will see during this simulation are:  
  • Nested States - Where the behavior of a State is specified through a composite element
  • StateMachineStates - Where the behavior of a State is specified by referencing an external StateMachine
  • Calling a separately defined behavior element from a State's entry operation
  • Tracing the value of a simulation variable using JavaScript
  • Sending of Triggers to transition from the current State
  • Signals that require arguments to be specified when firing
  • Transitions that can be fired from any child State by sending a Trigger

Terry works in a public facing role and has only recently started and during his induction he viewed the agency's standard operating procedures through the Pro Cloud Server. Yukiko works for a systems integrator and has to create an integration model between this agency and a range of external organizations and other Government agencies. She is delighted to be able to view component models, RESTful APIs and payload information. She cannot believe she doesn't have to wait for out-of-date documentation anymore and she can read it all in her own time on her Smart Phone. She enters a search for the RESTful Web APIs.

Diagram Overview - Out of the Office This deployment diagram describes the scenario of people working away from the office and their cable or wireless based LAN connections. Working on the train, bus or at the airport lounge or from a home office, or even in the park - anywhere there is an Internet connection. The Pro Cloud Server allows an office worker to connect to an Enterprise Architect repository from an EA Client on a notebook or desktop or from a Web Browser on any type of device including: Smart Phones, Tablets, Notebooks and Desktops and via a VPN or an Internet connection. Working through a Web Browser a worker can Browse and Contribute to the model, working through the EA Client they can also Author content as if they were sitting at their office desk.

elements.name: Author
elements.notes: An author is the writer who created the work, a particular item may have more than one author and it is possible that the author for a particular title is unknown or does not want to be known then it is said that the author is antonymous.

elements.name: Cart Item
elements.notes: An item that a user has selected and placed into a Shopping Cart, these form a discrete subset of the items in the catalogue but there may be multiple copies of the same item in the same cart.

elements.name: Catalog
elements.notes: A register of items that can be sold that includes a range of details and properties the nature of which depends on the type of item. The catalogue is used to generate the product pages on the web site and also to determine selling rules and conditions.

elements.name: Item
elements.notes: This represents a discrete and catalogued entity that can be purchased through the store. This was traditionally a book or more generally a title but on-line extended selling has meant the definition has needed to be generalized so as to represent the range of things being sold.

elements.name: Line Item
elements.notes: The accounting representation of a the cart items that the user selected in a given session. These items together make up the order.

elements.name: Order

elements.name: Publisher

elements.name: Review
elements.notes:
A critical appraisal either formal or informal written and made available to assist potential purchasers in deciding on whether the item is suitable for their needs. There are two main types of reviews:  
  • Editorial Reviews - written by the bookstore.
  • Customer Reviews - written by people who have already purchased the book.

elements.name: Shopping Cart
elements.notes: A shopping cart is an online equivalent of the carts provided by supermarkets that can be wheeled through a number of aisles allowing customers to collect the items they want to purchase.

elements.name: Business Case - Extended Selling
elements.notes: The Extended Selling Business Case has been developed by the Strategy and Innovation team and investigates the CEO's idea of extending the product lines from books and titles to other products.

elements.name: Corporate Reports
elements.notes:
It is envisioned that many of the existing corporate customers that purchase titles from the bookstore will extend their purchases to other items such as stationary and office equipment. The platform will provide corporate reports that details the sales over a chosen period and will include details such as:  
  • Items Purchased
  • Purchase Dates
  • Tax Rates
  • Discounts
  • Authority
The reports will be disseminated based on the customers' preferences and will include post, email, sales portal.

elements.name: REQ00276 - The system will allow a party to define their report preferences
elements.notes:
Users will have a facility to define their preference for a report including delivery options. Report preferences will be able to be set at three different levels:
  • Organization
  • Department (Section)
  • Individual
Security will restrict access to the various levels; for some preference the precedence will be set from Organization to Individual, and for others it will be the reverse, from Individual to Organization.

elements.name: REQ00277 - The system will automatically generate and disseminate reports
elements.notes: The report generation and dissemination will be orchestrated by a scheduler that will ensure the reports are generated and disseminated in accordance with the preferences set by the appropriate party.

elements.name: REQ00278 - The system will aggregate sales from an organization
elements.notes:
The reports at all levels will display aggregates:
  • A User report - will aggregate purchases for all items..
  • A Department report - will aggregate purchases for all users.
  • An Organization report - will aggregate purchases for all departments.
The electronic version will contain collapsible regions so that the details can be hidden.

elements.name: Jenny Tomikano
elements.notes: Jenny is a 32 year old mother of three who lives in California. She was slow to embrace the Internet but since her kids were born, and time is a limited commodity, she has become the local expert in on-line shopping. She is tech savvy and doesn't waste time with slow or poorly designed web sales platforms. She knows what she wants and generally get it.

elements.name: FEA025 - Social Media Integration
elements.notes:
The system provides customizable integration with Social Media including the following social platforms:  
  • Facebook
  • Google+
  • Twitter
  • Pinterest
Harnessing relevant and interesting information and keeping the social pulse so customers can benefit from these cross platform aggregations.

elements.name: REQ00279 - The system must provide a customizable platform independent hub
elements.notes: The system must provide a customizable hub that allows adapters to be added for the various social media platforms. Generic adapter should be used wherever possible and only when required new ones should be created.

elements.name: REQ00280 - The system must perform aggregation at a semantic level
elements.notes: The aggregation of the social media data must be able to occur at a semantic (meaning) layer. This will allow near human level associations to be made between content items in the registered platforms.  For example the alignment of lexicographically disparate content that has the same semantic intent.

elements.name: REQ00281 - The system must be able to determine relevance based on pre-set criteria
elements.notes: Given the large volume of social media information that could potentially served to a customer it is critical that it is relevant to the audience and that this relevance can be assigned with pre-set criteria for a given audience segment

Baselines

Enterprise Architect provides a facility to capture a 'Baseline' (snapshot) of a model branch at a particular point in time, for comparison with the Package state at a later time.
To access the Baselines facility, from the 'Design' ribbon select the option 'Model > Manage > Manage Baselines', or press Ctrl+Alt+B.
Baselines are generally used in conjunction with the Compare utility. To view an example, first select the 'Baselines' Package (the Package that contains this diagram), then open the 'Manage Baselines' dialog and click on the 'Show Differences' button to perform a comparison.
Alternatively, use this link to view images depicting each of those windows.

When performing a comparison between the current model state and one of the saved baselines, simply select the required baseline, then click on 'Show Differences'.
Note that it is also possible to load baselines from other Enterprise Architect projects.

Element Discussions
Discussion History

To open the 'Discussion History' view, from the ribbon select the option:
'Start > Collaborate > Discuss > Discussion History'.
This image provides an example of the Discuss & Review History window.  The list has been filtered, using the Filter Bar, to show only those discussions topics whose status is 'Open'.
Element Discussions

To open the Discuss & Review window from the ribbon, select the option:
'Start > Collaborate > Discuss > Discuss'.
This image is an example of the Discuss & Review window.
The element 'Anne_Actor' has been selected in the model, so the discussions relating to that element are displayed in the Discuss & Review window.

Enterprise Architect provides facilities for attaching any number of discussion threads to elements within your model.
The Discuss & Review window allows you to create, read and reply to discussions for the selected element, whilst the Discuss & Review - History window lists all discussions, with various options for sorting and filtering.
Using the 'Discuss' tab of the dockable Discuss & Review window, you can review and participate in discussions on different elements simply by clicking on each element in turn; the Discuss & Review window immediately switches to the discussion of the new selected element.
The Discuss & Review - History window, on the other hand, lists all discussions on all elements within the model, with options for sorting and filtering the display.  There is also an option to edit (contribute to) the selected discussion thread.
Both windows can be accessed through the 'Start > Collaborate > Discuss' ribbon option.

The Gantt Views

The Gantt View is a tool that charts the allocation of resources to elements in a project, Package or diagram. There are a number of different Gantt charts available:
  • The Project Gantt View - used to view elements across the entire repository
  • Personal Gantt View - used to view task assignments for the current user, based on resource allocations
  • Diagram Gantt View - used to display the allocation of resources to the elements in a given diagram
  • Package Gantt View - used to display the allocation of resources to the elements contained in a selected Package

• Project Gantt View - from the 'Construct' ribbon, select the option 'Resource Management > Gantt'
  • Personal Gantt View - from the 'Start' ribbon, select the option 'Personal > My Gantt'
  • Diagram Gantt View - from the 'Design' ribbon, select the option 'Diagram > Views > Gantt View', or right-click on a diagram and choose 'Switch View | Switch to Gantt View'
  • Package Gantt View - from the 'Design' ribbon, select the option 'Package > Gantt View', or right-click on a Package and choose 'View as Gantt'
Note: You can also set the 'Always open as Gantt' option in the Diagram Properties.

This will be used to present to various publishers in order to gain final funding to complete the project.

elements.name: Location 1 -  Puzzles
elements.notes:
This task relates to creating a set of puzzles for the first area the player will encounter.

All main puzzles that affect the storyline must take into account the abilities and items the player will have access to at the time they are encountered as to not hinder the players progress through the main story.

Side puzzles need not be linear, some sections will require the player to return to in order to pass the puzzle as they will not have the required skill or item. This can include a puzzle for the main story as long as the player is guided to this location after having gained the required skills/items.

Team Review

Enterprise Architect's Model Library facility provides a forum and document repository in which team members can discuss and document the development and progress of a project. The Model Library has two main displays - the Library window and the 'Team Document' tab (a document editor window).
The Library window is used to create new Categories and Topics and to delete messages; you operate on it by selecting options from the context menu.
The 'Team Document' tab is a document editor, created as a tab in the main work area.  It is used to create, view, edit, print, and comment on Documents, and to create and maintain the descriptions of Topics and Categories.
To open the Library window:  from the 'Start' ribbon, select the option 'Collaborate > Model Library'.
To open the Team Document tab (editor), double-click an item in the Library window (such as a Category, Topic or Document), or from the context menu of the Library window, select 'Show Contents' or 'New Document'.

There are three key areas in which Enterprise Architect supports publishing of model information. There are facilities for:
  • generating documentation from your model, as RTF reports, HTML reports or PDF documents
  • exchanging part or all of a model with other tools or with other EA projects
  • publishing MDG Technologies that have been developed within your model.

Design Patterns

To publish a Design Pattern you first must model the Pattern as a diagram within Enterprise Architect.
Once the diagram of the Pattern is complete, it can then be published into an XML file.

To publish the Pattern, open the diagram, then select the ribbon option:
'Specialize > Technologies > Publish Technology > Publish Diagram as Pattern'.

The published Pattern can subsequently be imported into any Enterprise Architect model as a Resource that can be dropped onto a diagram to recreate the Pattern.

The design pattern known as 'Decorator' is shown here.

It was created from an example in the GoF book "Design Patterns - Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software" by Gamma et al.

It was dropped onto this diagram from the Resources folder
'Patterns | GoF Structural Patterns'.

You can publish this diagram as a Pattern yourself and then import it as a Resource; perform these steps:
  1. Select the ribbon option 'Specialize > Technologies > Publish Technology > Publish Diagram as Pattern'
In the 'Publish Diagram as Pattern' dialog,
  1. Specify a distinct pattern name, such as 'myPattern'
  2. Specify a suitable location and filename such as 'C:\temp\myPattern.xml'
  3. Click on the OK button.
In the 'Resources' tab of the Browser window,
  1. Right-click on the Patterns folder and select 'Import Pattern'.
  2. Specify the filename that you used to publish the pattern.
  3. Click on the OK button.
Finally, create a new Package with an empty diagram. From the 'Resources' tab of the Browser window, drag and drop 'myPattern' onto the empty diagram. Delete the Package and its contents when finished.

Help Modeling

The packages displayed on this diagram, show an example of the model components that are typically used in creating a Help System model.  This example is a copy of an early draft of the actual Enterprise Architect Help topic "Help System Authoring".  The generated content has been published to: https://sparxsystems.com/enterprise_architect_user_guide/16.1/model_publishing/help_system_authoring.html

The model fragment is presented here, so you can explore the model yourself and examine its structure. You can also experiment with generating file sets from a Help model. You can generate either HTML files or PDF files from the same model. To generate HTML files: In the Browser window, right-click on the package "Help System Authoring", then choose the menu option "Generate Help on Current Item". Select an existing folder on your file system as the Output Folder, then click on "Generate". View the generated files using a web browser. To generate PDF files: Select the package "Help System Authoring" in the Browser window, then press "F8". The "Generate Documentation" dialog will display. Specify a filename for the file to generate. Use a folder that already exists on your file system and specify a file extension of ".pdf". Select the 'User Guide' template in the 'Template' drop-down list and 'User Guide Styles' in the 'Stylesheet' drop-down list. Click on "Generate". Once the generation is complete, click on "View" to open the file in a PDF viewer.

elements.name: Help System Authoring
elements.notes:
Enterprise Architect enables you to provide support for the users of the models, systems and processes you develop, using the Help System Model. This is a simple-to-use model that has a number of facilities for creating a structure of Help topics to document your model or system as extensively and as deeply as you require. These facilities include:
  • A Help Profile, defining the Help stereotypes, Tagged Values and the Help page of the Diagram Toolbox
  • A Help Perspective (accessed from the Management Perspective group)
  • Help model patterns that provide a starting point for you to create your own Help model using stereotyped elements from the Help Profile
  • Help generation templates
  • A basic CSS file that you can modify and extend as required
  • An HTML generator and a PDF generator, building documentation from the same source Help model
HTML files generated from your Help model, can be deployed on the Internet through your own website or on your local file system and then viewed with any Web browser. PDF documents can also be generated for those users wanting to access a more 'linear' version of the Help. The final section of this topic provides a brief explanation of how you generate and view the Help pages you are creating.

elements.name: Use of the Help System Elements
Authoring Help System Content
elements.notes:
The Enterprise Architect Help System model provides all the structure, formatting and styles you require to immediately create and generate Help topics that resemble the Enterprise Architect Help itself. You can then edit the CSS file and the templates to tailor the output to reflect your organizations own standards and presentation.
The format of the source Help material is largely controlled by Enterprise Architect, and then interpreted by the HTML and PDF generators as defined by the templates and CSS file. There are, however, various formats and styles you can impose as you write your Help text, and these are discussed in the sections of this topic.

elements.name: Generating Help Files
elements.notes:
During the Help Authoring process and upon completion it is important to generate the content you are working on into HTML and/or PDF form. This allows you to view how your material will appear to the final consumer, and to check for obvious formatting errors, omissions and other mistakes. It is best to generate both formats as there are subtle differences between the outputs. 
A good PDF document will be easy to read, well formed and of a consistent look and feel. Ensure paragraph spacing, image placement, heading placement and other formatting issues are checked and corrected if necessary. The same approach should be used for HTML with the additional necessity of checking hyperlinks and other web-only constructs. 
When generating for testing purposes the item being worked on can be created on the local file system and reviewed. After the inclusion of your material in the actual 'Help System' proper, the next generation of the full HTML Help or PDF document library can be updated to include your topics.

elements.name: Help Template Files
elements.notes:
Enterprise Architect makes use of a series of template files when generating HTML content from your Help model.  Each of the template files contains some formatting information, as well a some placeholders where generated content will be inserted.
As each model element is rendered, the corresponding template file is loaded into memory and the element data is substituted into the appropriate placeholders.  The page content is built up as each element is rendered, until finally, the page content is substituted into the corresponding placeholder in the 'master template' file.
There is a specific template file that corresponds to each type of element available in the Help model, as well as two sample 'master template' files.
All of these template files are provided as a part of Enterprise Architect and will be copied to a sub-folder in your specified output folder the first time you generate files from your Help model.
It is expected that you will customize the master template file to suit your own needs, however, it is far less likely that you will need to modify the element template files.
You should have a working knowledge of HTML before attempting to customize any of the template files.

elements.name: Help System Tables
elements.notes:
Tables provide a convenient way of presenting information to people; the Help Model helps you to set up a range of different types of table to suit different purposes, such as defining the meanings of icons, or describing stages in a process, or describing numbered steps in a procedure. The HTML and PDF generators support definitions for 2-column or 3-column tables. The two generators determine how to render tables using different rules. The HTML generator operates on business rules stored in code. The PDF generator works on element stereotypes, each stereotype being rendered via a fixed RTF template:
  • The element's stereotype determines the table layout, column width and fields used; all of these settings are fixed
  • The layout applies to the entire table, so all rows of a table must follow the same configuration
